subject: Dedicated capacity follow-up: GPU family, TPS targets & token distribution
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@quantflow.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity follow-up: GPU family, TPS targets & token distribution

Hi Olivia — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can size a dedicated pool that matches QuantFlow's production profile.

Summary of options we discussed:
- Hosted API: fastest to start, shared capacity, good for small spikey traffic.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): required for specific compliance controls (we can scope if needed).

For dedicated sizing we need a short confirmation on these items (see inline):
1) TPS targets: you mentioned a baseline of ~60 TPS per feature and peaks up to ~120 TPS during batch runs — can you confirm peak sustained vs short bursts and whether spikes are owned by a single endpoint or many?
2) Typical prompt length / token mix: we need 95th/median token lengths for both prompts and completions. If you can attach a small sample payload or token_profile.csv, that will speed our throughput modeling.
3) Concurrency and latency SLOs: do you need 95th percentile latency <=200ms? or is 500ms acceptable for some endpoints?
4) Preferred GPU families or constraints: any org policy for A100 vs H100 vs L4? If unspecified we'll model both cost/perf options.

Attachments: quantflow_token_profile.csv (empty template) and redwood_gpu_options.pdf (brief GPU family guidance).

Proposed next steps:
- If you can reply with the token sample and TPS clarifications, we will run a preliminary sizing and share a recommended pool mix (GPU types + instance counts) + estimated monthly cost.
- Optional technical deep-dive with our infra engineer (Karthik) — 30 min — to go over edge cases (KV cache, prefix caching, burst policies).

Thanks — Jordan

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

From: Olivia Chen <olivia@quantflow.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Chen <mark.chen@quantflow.ai>
Date: 2027-10-19T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity follow-up: GPU family, TPS targets & token distribution

Thanks Jordan — appreciated the clear recap. Quick answers below; Mark (our infra lead) is cc'd for any deeper infra specifics.

1) TPS: our primary search/qa endpoint averages ~45 TPS during business hours (US east). We see short-running background batches that push to ~110 TPS sustained for 10–12 minute windows; those batches are routed to a single service (same endpoint).
2) Token mix: typical user prompts are 12–24 tokens; completions average 40–120 tokens depending on the generation mode. We'll attach a small sample log (separate file) — attaching a CSV of 1k request rows.
3) Latency: we're targeting 95th <= 250ms for OSS user-facing calls; 500ms is tolerable for batch jobs.
4) GPU preference: no strict policy, but cost is a consideration. We prefer to evaluate H100 for peak-critical endpoints and L4 for cheaper scale-out where latency tolerance is higher.

Also, we are likely to need a VPC/private option for parts of our dataset later this year — curious how that changes the sizing/cost assumptions.

Olivia
Head of Product | QuantFlow
olivia@quantflow.ai | +1 650-555-2219

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@quantflow.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-19T14:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity follow-up: GPU family, TPS targets & token distribution

Thanks for the details, Olivia — that's very helpful. A couple of clarifying follow-ups before we size: 

- For the batch windows (110 TPS sustained): are requests evenly parallelizable across many short sequences, or are they large single-sequence generations that need more memory/KV capacity? That affects instance memory sizing and whether we favor H100 with larger memory vs more L4 nodes.
- Do you expect the 110 TPS windows to be predictable (scheduled nightly/batch) or irregular spikes driven by traffic? If scheduled, we can propose autoscale + burst policies to reduce cost.
- For the VPC need you mentioned: is the requirement data-in-transit only, or do you need customer-managed key material (KMS/HSM) and private control plane?

If helpful, Karthik can do a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through inferred request shapes and show two config options: (A) H100-heavy pool sized for 95th-latency production SLO; (B) mixed pool (H100 + L4) with autoscale/burst to hit cost targets.

--
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0186

Perfect, thanks Olivia — this is exactly what we needed. Next items / proposed timeline: 

1) Please upload the 1k request CSV to the Drive link above (or reply with the file) so we can run a token-distribution analysis. We'll use that to model steady-state pod counts and memory pressure per GPU.
2) Karthik to run two quick sizing sketches (H100-only and mixed H100+L4) and produce a cost/latency comparison in 48 hours.
3) We'll include VPC-onboarding notes in the cost delta; Neha to capture whether you need customer-managed KMS and private control plane (short checklist below).

Redwood action items (we own):
- Sizing sketches + recommended instance counts (48 hours)
- Sample YAML for canary + burst autoscale policy for scheduled batches
- Pricing delta for Private (VPC) vs Dedicated-hosted variants

QuantFlow action items:
- Upload sample CSV of requests (1k rows) or confirm shared Drive link
- Confirm whether KMS/HSM or private control plane is required for VPC onboarding

I'll propose a 30-min technical scoping slot for Thu 10/21 10:00–10:30 PT — does that work for Mark and your infra team?

Thanks — looking forward.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
